thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: increased OOMs observed from serving-runtime on cluster-gpu-us-east-2, pods flapping (count=12) — severity: P1. Investigate paging/allocator fragmentation path (kv-cache + paged-attn).

maya (oncall): seeing the same - charts show memory creeping then sudden OOM on worker pools serving r-llama-uncased. Node flaps started ~10m ago. I'll take first responder.

arjun (eng-runtime): thanks. initial hypothesis: paged-attention allocator fragmentation + KV cache growth leading to slow memory creep. We shipped allocator tweak last week that changed free list binning; might be related.

lina (sre): pinging infra to check if any noisy jobs started. Also, are customer-facing routes impacted?

priya (support): we have 3 customer reports of 503s in last 12m — small batch inference requests timing out. Flagging enterprise customers on Dedicated.

tom (eng-runtime): attaching last logs snippet: ```
[runtime] ERROR cuda: out of memory when allocating 256MB
[allocator] warn: free bin fragmentation, available_free: 1.2GB, largest_contiguous: 80MB
[kv-cache] info: shard-7 items=1.2M, mem=9.8GB, evictions=0
container crash: runtime_worker_24 pid=24112 signal=SIGABRT
```

maya (oncall): quick mitigation plan suggestions: 1) route new traffic to smaller model variants; 2) disable aggressive caching on affected routes; 3) drain worst nodes and restart runtime pods with empty KV; 4) lift canary fallback to v-low-memory. Which can we do immediately?

arjun (eng-runtime): immediate actions we can do now: - reduce per-request max_context to 1024 for the heavy routes (config route override) - toggle kv-cache eviction to aggressive (ttl=60s) via runtime feature-flag - push a rolling restart of runtime pods on the two most-flappy nodes (cordon -> drain -> restart)

lina (sre): I'll cordon node-gpu-12 and node-gpu-14. Starting drain for node-gpu-12 now. Command: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-12 && kubectl drain node-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -l app=runtime`.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: runtime-config-change (kv-evict-ttl) by arjun — ID: dpl-2026-03-15-492.

priya (support): telling affected customers: "We're investigating intermittent 503s tied to GPU worker restarts; temporary mitigation active; we'll follow up in 30m with status."

maya (oncall): arjun, can you flip the kv-eviction flag and reduce context on the route? Then we can watch OOMs.

arjun (eng-runtime): flipping now. Patch: `feature.kv_evict_ttl=60s`; `route.r-llama-uncased.max_context=1024`. Rolling config to 8 pods.

[~1m later]
arjun (eng-runtime): kv-eviction toggle applied, context limit applied. Observability: memory growth slope reduced but still fragmenting - largest contiguous chunk remains ~70-90MB on affected pods.

maya (oncall): Lina, how's drain progress?

lina (sre): node-gpu-12 drained, pods rescheduled. node-gpu-14 still terminating one pod (runtime_worker_24) — it keeps OOMing during shutdown. We'll force delete after 10s if stuck.

maya (oncall): good. Tom, can you run a lightweight heap analysis on a restarted pod to detect fragmentation (pmap + /proc/<pid>/smaps)?

tom (eng-runtime): running `pmap -x <pid>` and `grep -A5 "VmRSS\|RssAnon" /proc/<pid>/status`. Also capturing jemalloc stats: `je-malloc-stats`. Pasting relevant lines: ```
jemalloc: allocated=10.4GB active=11.8GB metadata=280MB
arena[3]: small_unmapped=120MB dirty=30MB
fragmentation_ratio=1.13
largest_free_block=82MB
```

arjun (eng-runtime): jemalloc shows many small free runs - free lists are fragmented. The allocator's merging heuristic apparently doesn't coalesce pages across the paged-attention mappings correctly once KV cache pins lots of small K/V entries. Need an allocator hotfix to force coalescing or zeroing small free runs.

maya (oncall): can we hotpatch to runtime to prefer returning free pages to OS sooner or change page size? Risky in prod. Any safer quick wins?

arjun (eng-runtime): safer: reduce kv-shard memory cap per process (cap=6GB) and enable per-request KV bypass for streaming calls (no caching). That will free up contiguous ranges over time. Also set runtime env `PAGED_ATTEN_DISABLE_REUSE=1` to avoid re-using fragmented slabs temporarily.

lina (sre): doing kv-shard cap change via config map now. If this doesn't drop usage within 10-15m we'll schedule controlled rolling restart to defragment address space.

deploy-bot: ConfigMap updated: runtime-kv-shards -> cap=6GB by lina — rollout started (rollout-id: cm-9876).

[~12m later]
arjun (eng-runtime): metrics update: pod memory trending down in most nodes. OOM count reduced from 12->2 in the last 10m. However one pod still shows repeated small OOMs on CUDA allocations of 32-128MB - looks like GPU memory fragmentation separate from host: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY`.

maya (oncall): we should escalate GPU-specific fragmentation to infra team; also consider draining the node and migrating to different GPU type if telemetry suggests driver issue.

tom (eng-runtime): collecting `nvidia-smi -q` from the problematic node; log: ```
GPU 0: FB Memory Usage: Total 24576 MiB, Used 24450 MiB, Free 126 MiB
processes: many small allocations, no single large free chunk
```

arjun (eng-runtime): that's the problem — user-level allocator ended up scattering allocations and GPU memory is highly fragmented. For immediate relief: reduce concurrency on the pod (threads=1) to lower concurrent allocations, and restart process to release GPU VRAM back to driver.

lina (sre): I'm scheduling restart of the problematic pod after current request drains. Will cordon node if restarts fail.

priya (support): update for customers: "We've implemented routing to lower-memory models and are actively restarting affected workers; service degradation should improve in the next 15-30 minutes. We'll update again at 30min."

maya (oncall): status update for incident: mitigation in progress, visible reduction in OOMs, customer impact reduced but not fully resolved. Severity remains P1 until stable. Action items: 
- arjun/tom: continue profiling and prepare allocator patch (force coalesce + aggressive free-to-OS)
- lina: continue node drains + coordinate infra for GPU fragmentation checks
- maya: call with SRE in 30m for handoff update
- priya: keep customers informed

arjun (eng-runtime): creating a debug branch for allocator fix, will run unit/bench tests. Proposed short-term patch: `coalesce_on_free=true` and `deferred_arena_release_ms=5000`. Will test in canary.

tom (eng-runtime): capturing heapprofiles and core dumps to s3: `s3://redwood-debug/incident-1769501123/`. Core and jemalloc dumps uploaded.

maya (oncall): handing off to night oncall (arjun will be 1st responder), I'll update the incident channel and move this thread to "incident-handoff" in 15m. Please update here with any regression.

priya (support): noted. I'll prepare a consolidated customer update once we see full stabilization.

incident-bot: Incident P1 ongoing — runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/paged-attn-frag. Next update expected by 1769502923.

arjun (eng-runtime): final note for handoff: do NOT roll back last week's allocator change (it fixed unrelated perf regressions). Instead, deploy the targeted coalesce patch after bench sign-off. Also consider enabling `fallback-model` for enterprise customers as pre-approved emergency step.

maya (oncall): thanks team. continuing watch until handoff.

[thread end]
